title: Chapter 2: Earth : Shape, Size and Motions

blocks.content: The true shape of the Earth is a Geoid, meaning an Earth-like shape, which is slightly flattened at the poles and bulges at the equator.

rows: Spinning of the Earth around its own imaginary axis
Movement of the Earth around the Sun along an elliptical orbit
Counter-clockwise (West to East) along the orbit
Causes day and night, deflections of winds and ocean currents
Causes changing seasons and variations in the duration of day and night

items: Distinguish between axial inclination angles: 23.5° from the vertical perpendicular versus 66.5° from the orbital plane.
Summer Solstice occurs on June 21 (longest day in Northern Hemisphere), while Winter Solstice occurs on December 22.
Perihelion (Earth closest to the Sun) occurs around January 3, whereas Aphelion (Earth farthest from the Sun) occurs around July 4.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The true shape of the Earth is an oblate spheroid or 'Geoid', which is flattened at the poles and bulges at the equator.
The axis of the Earth is an imaginary line tilted at an angle of 66.5° to its orbital plane and 23.5° relative to the perpendicular.
Rotation is the spinning of the Earth on its axis from West to East, completed in 24 hours, which causes day and night.
Revolution is the movement of the Earth around the Sun in an elliptical orbit, taking 365¼ days and giving rise to seasons.
Equinoxes occur on March 21 and September 23, when the Sun's direct rays fall on the equator resulting in equal length of day and night worldwide.
